title: How Fast Is Earth’s Field Slipping?

segments.text: Did you know Earth’s magnetic field is slowly slipping?
In 2019, the field’s magnitude ranged from 30,000 to 60,000 nT across the surface.
The dipole strength has been decreasing at about 6.3% per century over the last two centuries.
A 2021 study suggests the field cycles every 200 million years due to deep Earth processes.
The current intensity is about average for the last 7,000 years, meaning the current rate of change is not unusual.
The field’s decline is just another tick in the same cycle.
The field’s strength is steady, not a runaway collapse.
